https://www.dw.com/en/colombia-dozens-ki.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IZRh Locals and emergency personnel in Pereira, Colombia rushed to help comb the rubble of collapsed buildings Image: REUTERS Advertisement A powerful earthquake shook western Colombia early on Monday morning. Around six hours after the quake struck, Colombia's president said that 111 people had been confirmed dead around the country. Rescue teams were working to free residents after buildings collapsed in Cali and other cities. The epicenter was on the eastern tip of the Choco province on Colombia's Pacific coast. The mayor of Cali said that 'at least 20 structures' collapsed in the quake Image: Reuters TV/REUTERS What is the latest? Colombia's newly-inaugurated President Abelardo de la Espriella said that he had personally taken charge of the government's response to the emergency. He said that locating anyone still potentially trapped was the highest priority for rescuers and declared a national state of emergency. "As of 12:30 [local time], the toll stood at 111 dead and 87 injured, with 1,575 homes damaged, 37 completely destroyed, 61 buildings collapsed, and 18 health centers and 52 schools damaged," de la Espriella said from Bogota. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US was "closely monitoring" the situtation and stood "ready to support the people of Colombia." What's happening on the ground? The mayor of Cali, Alejandro Eder, said that at least 20 buildings had collapsed, in some cases with people trapped inside. "Residents of Cali, we currently have at least 20 collapsed structures in the city with people trapped inside; we are already managing this emergency alongside all of Cali's rescue agencies," Eder said on Instagram, posting an accompanying video statement. "I have requested support — specifically rescue personnel — from the mayors of Bogota and Medellin." Authorities in the Valle del Cauca, whose capital city is Cali, later said that at least 27 people had died in the quake. Officials in Risaralda said that 40 people had died across the state, at least 18 of them in the capital Pereira based on earlier comments from the mayor. And the mayor of Manizales, Jorge Eduardo Rojas, said in a radio interview that two people were killed in his city, in the Caldas region not far northeast of Pereira. Residents in Cali tried to rush to safety in the aftermath of Monday's earthquake Image: Santiago Saldarriaga/AP Photo/picture alliance The governor of the Choco region where the quake's epicenter was located, Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi, said there were four dead and 69 wounded in her district as of late morning local time. Colombia's civil aviation authority reported damage at six relatively minor airports and said flights were suspended while it was examined. "Damage is reported at the airports of Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago, and Buenaventura. For safety reasons, air operations at these terminals remain suspended until structural damage to the infrastructure is assessed," it wrote online, later adding Cali's airport to this list. What do we know about the quake's size and location? The US Geological Survey (USGS) measured the quake at magnitude 7.4. Colombia's national authority at first logged a smaller figure but later revised its reading up to 7.4 as well. The epicenter was located just south of the Tatama National Nature Reserve, near Choco's eastern state border. One of the towers at the Cathedral of Manizales was damaged by the quake Image: John Jairo Bonilla/AP Photo/picture alliance The epicenter was roughly equidistant from Colombia's three main cities, Bogota to its east, Medellin to its north and Cali to its south. The closest major population center, Cartago, is home to about 140,000 people and around 30 kilometers (roughly 20 miles) from the quake's epicenter. The USGS said the quake was also quite deep, striking around 107 kilometers below the ground. It estimated that most of the western half of Colombia would feel the tremors . Tremors could also be felt in neighboring Ecuador to the south, and to the north and east in Panama and Venezuela. USGS also recorded a fairly large aftershock, at magnitude 5.0, a little under an hour after the main quake. The so-called Ring of Fire — the world's most active belt of tectonic plates and volcanoes encircling the Pacific Ocean — runs along Colombia's coastline not far from the epicenter of Monday's quake. Photograph: Ben Birchall/PA Reform UK Helen Jenner unveiled as Reform UK’s new leader in Wales after arrest of Dan Thomas Nigel Farage dismisses loss of previous leader as ‘bump in the road’ and says party will ‘carry on as if nothing has happened’ Ben Quinn Political correspondent Mon 21 Sep 2026 12.54 EDT First published on Mon 21 Sep 2026 09.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nigel Farage dismissed the loss of Reform UK’s leader in Wales last week as a “bump in the road” as the party unveiled a replacement. Helen Jenner replaces Dan Thomas, who stood down last Tuesday after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviours. Jenner, who was previously the party’s deputy leader in Wales , narrowly beat her rival, Jason O’Connell, in a poll of its 33 Senedd members. She joined Farage on the steps of the Senedd, where he said Reform would “carry on as if nothing has happened”. Thomas announced last week that he was standing down after his arrest. He has been bailed and insists he has done nothing wrong. The former Tory councillor, who remains a member of the Welsh parliament, was only announced as Reform’s Welsh leader in February. Jenner is from Neath, near Port Talbot in south Wales, and represents Bangor Conwy Môn in the Senedd. Farage said of Thomas: “I am sorry for his personal difficulties that he is going through. No one’s life is ever seamless and I am quite sure he will come out of these before too long. “But it was pretty much untenable for him to continue as leader while he had these domestic disputes, so we very quickly and rapidly have moved to electing a new leader.” Farage confirmed that a new deputy leader in Wales would be elected, and said: “We will carry on as if nothing has happened, waiting for Dan who is going to stay a member of this place, to come back more actively with us. “We could have done without this bump in the road. But it has happened, we are making the best of it.” Thomas issued a statement last Tuesday after intense speculation about his future, saying that he had been reported to the police the previous weekend and was released without charge. “I stress that I have done nothing wrong, but I do not want the coming headlines to be a distraction from the fantastic work our Senedd team is doing in holding this government to account,” he said. Gwent police said a 45-year-old man from the Aberbargoed area had been arrested on 13 September “on suspicion of assault and engaging in controlling/coercive behaviour. He has been bailed pending further inquiries”. Thomas was perceived by some as having been parachuted in from Reform headquarters in London, which caused tensions, but Jenner is a Welsh speaker who has a track record of involvement with Farage’s parties and was elected to her new role by colleagues. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion She was a general election candidate for the Brexit party in 2019, and before that was a member of Ukip under Farage’s leadership. She takes charge at a time when Reform is hoping to consolidate and build on its gains in Senedd elections earlier this year. It emerged as the second largest party, largely at the expense of the Conservatives and Labour. She also takes charge after the party was rocked not only by the loss of Thomas but also the defection of another of its Senedd members, Sarah Cooper-Lesadd, to Plaid Cymru, which holds power. Her departure sparked fury in Reform, with the party’s deputy leader, Richard Tice, accusing her of lying to them about her political beliefs. Plaid Cymru said Cooper-Lesadd had been “honest about her political beliefs” and that her views had changed. Reform UK activists squabble over Farage’s plan for £72m donations Read more Cooper-Lesadd, who was elected to the Pen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg constituency, claimed that Reform UK was “far more interested in division, opposition and headlines than in finding solutions”. Before Thomas took up the post, Nathan Gill, who briefly led Reform UK in Wales in 2021, was jailed for 10 and a half years in 2025 for taking bribes to make statements in favour of Russia when he was an MEP.
